description: 30 labeled validator cases. Pure text, no video, no Whisper, no API calls. These are also the unit tests: written once, used twice (Rules.md §4). Every case is labeled with the GROUND TRUTH — what the creator actually did — not with what SponsorLint happens to return. A case SponsorLint gets wrong stays in the set and shows up in the metrics.

cases.note: The phrase is split across a Whisper segment break. Per-segment matching scores 70.6 and fails; the joined transcript scores 100.

rule.label: Sponsorship disclosure
rule.source_quote: The integration must be disclosed to viewers.

cases.note: KNOWN LIMITATION, labeled by ground truth. The creator did disclose the sponsorship, so the requirement was satisfied. 'Sponsored content' is not one of the five accepted phrasings in lint/disclosure.py, so SponsorLint reports FAIL and this counts as a False FAIL in the metrics. Left in deliberately: an eval that only contains cases the tool already handles is not a measurement.
